subject: Launch: cost/perf tuning intake for Voyage AI
messages:
From: Luca Romano <luca@voyage-ai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@voyage-ai.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch: cost/perf tuning intake for Voyage AI

Hi Hannah / Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with Redwood's latency and routing options. We're moving toward a soft launch in June and need help formalizing the cost/performance plan as part of onboarding. High-level ask: make a pragmatic set of defaults so our product team can ship without manual tuning, and a clear path for further optimization after launch.

A few quick details to help you scope:
- Expected traffic: 40k requests/day initially, spiking to ~120k/day within 2 months.
- Typical request size: 120-220 tokens in prompt, 60-120 tokens reply.
- SLA target: p95 latency < 400ms for interactive flows.
- Sensitive flows: NPI data; but non-sensitive for most usage.

Attached: voyage-tech-specs.pdf with API sample calls and sample prompt set. Can you propose an intake plan that covers batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profile recommendations, and routing fallbacks? Also include any procurement reminders (commit windows, required SLAs).

Best,
Luca
Product Lead — Voyage AI
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Luca Romano <luca@voyage-ai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@voyage-ai.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch: cost/perf tuning intake for Voyage AI

Thanks Luca — this is perfect context.

High-level intake + 3-week plan (draft):
1) Week 0 (Kickoff + data intake)
   - 60-minute kickoff with product + infra to gather workload patterns and security needs.
   - You supply a representative prompt set (you included sample-prompt-set.txt — thanks).
   - We validate sequence lengths and identify the 90th / 95th percentile lengths.
2) Week 1 (Baseline & quick wins)
   - Enable prefix/KV caching for deterministic prompts and recommend cache keys.
   - Configure conservative batching: target batch window 10ms, max batch size 8 for interactive flows; separate larger async queues for bulk.
   - Low-risk quant profile: 8-bit (int8) quant for non-sensitive models to reduce cost; keep fp16 for sensitive flows.
3) Week 2 (Tune & test)
   - Measure tail latency under synthetic traffic matching your spike scenarios.
   - Adjust batching window and dynamic autoscaling policies to hit p95 < 400ms.
   - Run A/B with a quantized variant + fallback routing to fp16 on error/regression.
4) Week 3 (Handoff & runbook)
   - Finalize routing policy: region preferences, cost-priority vs latency-priority routes, and automatic fallback chain.
   - Deliver a short runbook: how to adjust batch settings, cache TTLs, and quant profiles.

I've attached a ballpark estimate (redwood-cost-estimate-v1.xlsx) for the initial three-week engagement and a conservative monthly cost projection at expected volumes.

Open questions we need before kickoff:
- Are the sensitive flows isolated by route or mixed into the same API keys?
- What SLOs do you want for background (async) jobs vs interactive?
- Preferred kickoff window next week (Tue/Wed morning PST) — what works for your team?

I'll schedule a 60-minute slot tentatively for Tue 04/20 10:00 AM PT and send a calendar invite once you confirm.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Luca Romano <luca@voyage-ai.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch: cost/perf tuning intake for Voyage AI

Quick ops notes from my side (ops & routing):

- Routing policy: recommend a 3-tier chain for you:
  1) Low-latency route (fp16) in us-west for interactive. Failover ->
  2) Cost-optimized quantized variant (int8) in same region. Failover ->
  3) Cross-region fallback (us-east) if local capacity is exhausted.

- Batch tuning guidance: start conservative (batch window 10ms, max 8) then increase max_batch_size for async endpoints (up to 32) where latency allowed. We can add dynamic batch scaling by queue depth.

- Caching: prefix caching is high-impact if you have repeated system prompts / instruction templates. Use short TTLs (30s–5m) for interactive features where content refresh matters; longer TTLs for stable templates.

I'll bring logs-template + a small script to derive effective batch size from sample traffic during the kickoff.

—Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Luca Romano <luca@voyage-ai.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch: cost/perf tuning intake for Voyage AI

Adding model-level recommendations from an applied-ML perspective:

- Quantization profiles:
  * Start with post-training static quant (int8) on your non-sensitive models. That typically gives 2–3x cost reduction with negligible quality loss for completion workloads.
  * Reserve fp16 for flows that must preserve numeric fidelity (NPI / financial calcs).

- Warm cache strategy:
  * We can pre-warm KV caches for the most-common conversation starters; provide a ranked prompt list and we'll stage cache entries before peak windows.

- Evaluation plan:
  * Use your sample-prompt-set.txt plus a small holdout (~300 prompts) for quality regression checks. We'll run generation at baseline (fp16) vs int8 and produce a short quality report.

Attached: sample-prompt-set.txt (you already provided it) — please flag any prompts that must stay fp16.

Happy to discuss the evaluation thresholds (accept/reject) you want us to use.

—Monica
Implementation Lead, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

- Sensitive flows: currently mixed by endpoint but we can split by API key before kickoff; Elena (cc) will help on that.
- SLOs: interactive p95 < 400ms; background jobs p95 < 2s.
- Kickoff: Tue 04/20 10:00 AM PT confirmed for the product + infra + procurement folks.

We'll upload a cleaned prompt set with annotations and flag the top 100 prompts we want preserved in fp16. Procurement will review the redwood-cost-estimate-v1.xlsx and loop back on contract questions.

See you Tue.

Best,
Luca
